chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people on the last Friday of Sha'ban. He praised God and extolled Him, then said: 'O People! Indeed, a month has come upon you in which there is a night better than a thousand months. It is the month of Ramadan. God has made its fasting obligatory, and He has made praying one night in it voluntarily equal to the reward of one who prays voluntarily for seventy nights in other months. He has made whoever does one good deed in it equal to the reward of one who performs an obligatory duty in other months, and whoever performs an obligatory duty in it is like one who performs seventy obligatory duties in other months. It is the month of patience, and the reward of patience is Paradise. It is the month of sharing, and it is the month in which God increases the sustenance of the believer. Whoever feeds a fasting believer in it, for him is the freeing of a slave and forgiveness of his sins for what has passed.'

It was said to him: 'O Messenger of God, not all of us can afford to feed a fasting person.' He said: 'Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, is Generous. He will give this reward to whoever among you cannot afford more than a sip of milk to feed a fasting person, or a drink of fresh water, or a few dates, which is all he can afford. Whoever eases the burden on his slave in this month, God will ease his reckoning. It is a month whose beginning is mercy, whose middle is forgiveness, and whose end is acceptance and freedom from the Fire. You have no need in it to dispense with four qualities: two with which to please God, and two with which you have no need to dispense. As for the two with which to please God, they are testifying that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God. And as for the two with which you have no need to dispense, they are: asking God for your needs and Paradise, asking God for well-being, and seeking refuge in Him from the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific spiritual rewards and recommended practices for the month of Ramadan according to the Prophet's sermon in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this sermon underscores the unique spiritual economy of Ramadan, where voluntary acts equal obligatory ones and feeding a believer yields the reward of freeing a slave. The Prophet’s emphasis on accessible charity, such as a sip of milk or water, reflects the Shia scholarly focus on the democratization of spiritual merit, while the four essential practices link theological affirmation (Shahada) with practical supplication (Du'a) for divine acceptance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-135 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Abil Vard, on the authority of Abi Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), “God’s Prophet (MGB) addressed the people on the last Friday of the Arabic month of Sha’ban. He glorified God, praised Him, and then said, ‘O People! Indeed, a month has come in which each night is better than a thousand months. It is the month of Ramazan. God has prescribed fasting during it for you. Whoever stays up one night during that month and prays will receive the reward of one who has stayed up for seventy nights in other months and prayed. If you do any good deeds during that month, you will receive the reward of one who has done seventy good deeds in other months. If you perform any obligatory deeds in that month, your reward will be that of seventy similar cases in other months. It is the month of patience. The reward of patience is Paradise. Ramazan is the month of sympathy. It is the month in which God increases the share of a believer’s daily bread. Whoever feeds another believer (to break his fast) shall be given the rewardof freeing a slave. His past sins will also be forgiven.’

It was said to him (MGB), ‘O Prophet of God! Not all of us are able to feed another believer to break his fast!’ The Prophet (MGB) said, ‘Indeed the Honorable the Exalted God is generous. He would even give this reward to those of you who have nothing but a cup of milk, some juice, water or a date to feed another believer to break his fast. Whoever helps his slave with his duties during this month will be rewarded by God with an easier Reckoning. It is the month whose beginning is mercy, whose middle is forgiveness, and whose end is answering and releasing from the Fire. In it you are in need of four qualities: two qualities with which to please God, and two qualities with which you ask for the fulfillment of your own needs. The two qualities with which to please God are: testify that there is no god but God, and that I (Muhammad) am God’s Prophet. And the two qualities with which you may ask for the fulfillment of your needs are: Ask God for your needs and Paradise during that month. Also ask God to protect you from the Fire of Hell.’”
